In [8]:
#converting tree into IF THEN rules
#we go from root to each leaf and keep adding the condition, at the leaf we see which class has more samples
#binary columns threshold is 0.5 so left (<=0.5) = no and right = yes
def get_rules(model, labels, node=0, conditions=[]):
    t = model.tree_
    rules = []
    if t.children_left[node] == -1:   # -1 means its a leaf
        out = []
        for i in range(len(labels)):
            if t.value[node][i].argmax() == 1:
                out.append(labels[i] + " = yes")
            else:
                out.append(labels[i] + " = no")
        return ["IF " + " AND ".join(conditions) + " THEN " + ", ".join(out)]
    name = X.columns[t.feature[node]]
    if name == "Temperature":
        left = name + " <= " + str(round(t.threshold[node], 2))
        right = name + " > " + str(round(t.threshold[node], 2))
    else:
        left = name + " = no"
        right = name + " = yes"
    rules = rules + get_rules(model, labels, t.children_left[node], conditions + [left])
    rules = rules + get_rules(model, labels, t.children_right[node], conditions + [right])
    return rules

print("Combined tree rules")
for r in get_rules(tree, ["Inflammation", "Nephritis"]):
    print(r)
print()
print("Inflammation tree rules")
for r in get_rules(tree_inf, ["Inflammation"]):
    print(r)
print()
print("Nephritis tree rules")
for r in get_rules(tree_nep, ["Nephritis"]):
    print(r)

#cost complexity pruning , get all the alphas from pruning path and check each one with 5 fold cv
#stratifiedkfold doesnt take 2 labels so i made one combined label just for making folds like "10", "01"
combo = y["Inflammation"].astype(str) + y["Nephritis"].astype(str)
skf = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=552)
folds = list(skf.split(X, combo))

path = tree.cost_complexity_pruning_path(X, y)
alphas = path.ccp_alphas
print(alphas)

cvscores = []
for a in alphas:
    model = DecisionTreeClassifier(criterion="entropy", random_state=552, ccp_alpha=a)
    s = cross_val_score(model, X, y, cv=folds)   # with 2 labels both need to be correct to count
    cvscores.append([a, s.mean(), s.std()])
cvtable = pd.DataFrame(cvscores, columns=["alpha", "mean accuracy", "std"])
cvtable

Now answering the questions that were theoritical for problem 1

1 b Tree on whole data gets 100% on both labels , depth 4 and 6 leaves so the data is very clean and can be seperated fully temperature is the root at 37.95 then lumbar pain , micturition pains and urine pushing Nausea and burning of urethra are never used ,they dont give any extra info once the others are known

1 c rules are printed above. Combined tree rules are long because each leaf decides both labels together seperate trees are much easier Nephritis = yes IF Temperature > 37.95 AND Lumbar_pain = yes else no Inflammation = yes IF Urine_pushing = yes AND (Micturition_pains = yes OR Lumbar_pain = no) else no so nephritis is basically fever + back pain and inflamation is mostly the urine symptoms

1 d pruning path gave alphas 0, 0.10, 0.19, 0.23, 0.37 cv accuracy at alpha =0 is 1.0 and drops to 0.87 at the next alpha and keeps going down to 0.45 so cv picked alpha = 0 , full tree is already the minimal tree , every split is needed and removing any of them reduces accuracy Same for both seperate trees , alpha = 0 with 4 leaves and 3 leaves Final interpretable rule set is the per label one from 1 c (in the nephritis cell the label name prints as inflamation but its the nephritis rules)

#Every feature becomes or has mean 0 and standard deviation of 1 and then lasso again

#PCR = scale then prinicpal components then linear regression, M is chosen by cv
pcr = Pipeline([("scaler", StandardScaler()), ("pca", PCA()), ("lr", LinearRegression())])
grid = GridSearchCV(pcr, {"pca__n_components": list(range(1, 123))}, cv=kf, scoring="neg_mean_squared_error")
grid.fit(X_train, y_train)
M = grid.best_params_["pca__n_components"]
results["PCR"] = mean_squared_error(y_test, grid.predict(X_test))
print("M:", M)
print("PCR test MSE:", results["PCR"])

plt.plot(range(1, 123), -grid.cv_results_["mean_test_score"])
plt.axvline(M, color="red")
plt.xlabel("M")
plt.ylabel("cv MSE")
plt.title("PCR cv error vs number of components")
plt.show()

alphalist = [0, 1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10]
xgbgrid = GridSearchCV(xgb, {"reg_alpha": alphalist}, cv=kf, scoring="neg_mean_squared_error")
xgbgrid.fit(X_train, y_train)
results["XGBoost"] = mean_squared_error(y_test, xgbgrid.predict(X_test))
print("best alpha:", xgbgrid.best_params_["reg_alpha"])
print("XGBoost test MSE:", results["XGBoost"])

pd.DataFrame({"alpha": alphalist, "cv MSE": -xgbgrid.cv_results_["mean_test_score"]})

Now answering all the questions that were theoritical in problem 2

2 b 23 features have missing values , 22 are LEMAS police columns missing 1675 out of 1994 rows and OtherPerCap only 1 row missing i used median imputation , median is fit on train only and then used on test so test does not leak median instead of mean because lot of columns are skewed with outliers (counts like NumStreet) and median doesnt get pulled by them for LEMAS columns 84% values are imputed so they become almost constant , this is a limitation , other option was to drop them completely

2 c heatmap has big blocks of strong correlation , income columns together , family / two parent columns together and LEMAS ones together most correlated with target PctKids2Par (-0.74), PctIlleg (+0.74), PctFam2Par (-0.71) and racePctWhite (-0.68) so lot of multicolinearity which is why ridge , lasso and PCR make sense here

2 d CV table above, highest PctPolicAsian = 5.45 and lowest LemasSwFTFieldOps = 0.06 LEMAS columns at the bottom have low CV mostly because they were imputed with same value for most rows

2 e top 11 = PctPolicAsian, NumStreet, NumInShelters, NumIlleg, NumImmig, LemasPctOfficDrugUn, NumUnderPov, population, LemasSwornFT, numbUrban, HousVacant most of them are count features , almost all points are near 0 and few big cities are outliers (box plots show it , long tail above the whisker) NumIlleg , NumUnderPov and HousVacant show some positive trend with crime but others there is no clear pattern since everything is squished near 0 We cannot really judge significance from these plots , a plot is only one feature at a time and doesnt control for the other 121 , no p value or test either also high CV only means more spread , not that its related to target

2 f OLS test MSE = 0.01797

2 g Ridge lambda = 2.20 , test MSE = 0.01752 better than OLS because shrinking helps with multicolinearity

2 h LASSO raw lambda = 8.2e-05 kept 79 variables , test MSE = 0.01769 LASSO standarized lambda = 6.4e-04 kept 76 variables , test MSE = 0.01772 both almost the same , 75 variables common in both features in this data are already normalized 0-1 so standarizing doesnt change much , if features had very diffrent scales lasso would penalize them unfairly and then standarizing matters a lot lambda is different because coeffecients are on a different scale after standarizing

2 i PCR M = 97 , test MSE = 0.01837 , worst one needs 97 out of 122 components which means the high variance directions are not the ones that predict crime, PCA doesnt look at y when it makes components

2 j XGBoost with L1 , cv picked alpha =2 , test MSE = 0.01582 best overall , trees can catch non linear relations and interactions that linear models miss cv MSE lowest at alpha 2 and goes up at 10 so some L1 helps but too much underfits

Summary XGBoost 0.0158 < Ridge 0.0175 < LASSO 0.0177 ~= LASSO standarized 0.0177 < OLS 0.0180 < PCR 0.0184 all linear ones are very close , ridge/lasso small improvement over OLS , boosting is the clear winner
